name: Squirrel
description: Squirrel is a simple, self-contained HTTPS server for a munki software repository, with built-in TLS (Let's Encrypt or a supplied certificate) and HTTP Basic Authentication for the /repo/ endpoint. This installs Squirrel built from source alongside a fresh, empty munki repo skeleton (pkgs/pkgsinfo/catalogs/manifests) served over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate. There is no web admin UI here (unlike Munki-Repo/MunkiWebAdmin2) - manage the repo's contents with munkiimport/MunkiAdmin from a Mac or by editing files directly.

notes.text: Squirrel's own client is HTTP Basic Auth over TLS, with a self-signed certificate by default. Accept the certificate warning once, or replace /etc/ssl/squirrel/squirrel.{crt,key} with your own and restart the service, or switch to Let's Encrypt by editing -tls-domain in /etc/systemd/system/squirrel.service (requires a public DNS name and port 443 reachable from the internet).

The basic-auth password is generated during install and stored in /etc/squirrel/squirrel.env (SQUIRREL_BASIC_AUTH). The matching Authorization header for the munki client is also printed to the journal on every service start: journalctl -u squirrel -n 20.

The repo starts empty. Add packages with munkiimport or MunkiAdmin from a Mac (point it at /srv/munki_repo over rsync/scp/sshfs) and run makecatalogs there, since there is no in-container tooling to build catalogs.

Upstream (micromdm/squirrel) has had no tagged release since 2017 and no commits since 2021; this installs from the master branch, which is the only version with go.mod and the current cmd/squirrel flag set. Treat it as effectively unmaintained.
Squirrel also supports S3 and GCS as repo storage backends via the -provider flag; the default install uses the local filesystem at /srv/munki_repo.
